name: Dry Matter Intake Calculator
seoTitle: Dry Matter Intake Calculator — Formula & Results
seoDesc: Dry matter intake is how much feed an animal actually eats once the water is taken out, and it is the number nutritionists formulate against. Free dry matter
summary:
Dry matter intake is how much feed an animal actually eats once the water is taken out, and it is the number nutritionists formulate against. It returns dry matter intake, intake as % of body weight, target intake and feed offered, and the panel shows all of them at once.

This calculator estimates intake from body weight and feed type, converts as-fed weights into dry matter, and reports the percentage of body weight consumed. Press Calculate and the results appear in the grey boxes; after the first press they keep up with every edit, so there is no page to reload. Units are stated on every box and in every result, so a figure copied out of a protocol, a datasheet or a chart can be entered without converting it first.

sections.title: The formula behind the Dry Matter Intake
sections.html:
Dry matter intake = as-fed weight × dry-matter % ÷ 100; target intake ≈ 1.8–2.5% of body weight depending on feed

The symbols in the formula
SymbolWhat it stands forUnit
weightbody weightkg
asfedfeed offered, as fedkg/day
dmdry matter content of that feed%
intakedry matter actually eatenkg/day

sections.title: How do I use the Dry Matter Intake?
sections.html:
Every input sits in the same order the formula is written, so the page reads like the equation.

  1. Enter the values you already have. Every box accepts a decimal point and a minus sign; thousands separators are ignored.
  2. The grey boxes are results: they are worked out from your inputs and cannot be typed into.
  3. Press Calculate. The results fill in together, and from then on they follow every edit you make — there is no page to reload and nothing to submit.

sections.title: A worked example
sections.html:
Take the default values the page opens with: body weight of 500 kg, feed type set to 2.0, dry matter of the feed of 88%.

Substituting them into the formula gives dry matter intake of 12.32 kg/day, intake as % of body weight of 2.46%, target intake of 11 kg/day, feed offered of 14 kg/day.

Those numbers come from the same solver the page runs in your browser, not from an illustration, so typing different inputs moves the answer exactly as the arithmetic says.

sections.title: What does the result mean?
sections.html:
The number on its own is not a judgement. These are the bands most often used when the result is quoted in a paper, a report or a label:

How to read the result
ResultBandWhat it means
1.8 – 2.0% of BWConcentrate-heavyhigh-energy rations
2.0 – 2.2% of BWSilage-basedwet forage limits intake
2.2 – 2.5% of BWHay / pasturethe usual range for dry forage

  • Two feeds with the same as-fed weight can differ by a factor of three in dry matter: 10 kg of silage at 35% DM is 3.5 kg of dry matter, 10 kg of hay at 88% is 8.8 kg.

  • Intake as a percentage of body weight is how guidelines are written, so it is the number to compare against them.

  • Palatability, water access and fibre length all cap intake before the arithmetic does.

sections.title: What are the common mistakes?
sections.html:
These are the errors that account for almost every wrong answer people bring to this calculator:

  • Comparing a silage ration with a hay ration on an as-fed basis.
  • Assuming the dry matter percentage on the label is the same as the batch in the yard.
  • Feeding to a target intake without checking what is actually refused.

faq.q: What is a normal dry matter intake for cattle?
faq.a: About 2–2.5% of body weight on dry forage and 1.8–2% on high-concentrate rations.

faq.q: Why does dry matter matter more than as-fed weight?
faq.a: Because water has no nutritional value: dry matter is the part of the feed the animal can actually use.

faq.q: What does the Dry Matter Intake actually calculate?
faq.a: It returns dry matter intake, intake as % of body weight, target intake and feed offered. Each one is derived by the formula on this page, so you can check any figure by hand.

faq.q: Do I have to fill in every box?
faq.a: Fill in the ones you know. The result boxes are computed from them, so you never enter a value the formula can derive — and if you change an input, every result updates with it.

faq.q: Why is the answer different from the one in my protocol?
faq.a: Nearly always a unit or a rounding difference. This calculator works in the units printed next to each box, keeps full precision internally and only rounds for display, so recomputing from the rounded numbers on screen can differ in the last digit.

faq.q: Can I use it with the numbers straight from a datasheet?
faq.a: Yes. Every box states its unit, and nothing is converted behind your back, so a figure copied from a datasheet, a kit insert or a protocol goes in as printed.
